newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan railway group to unveil big office complex.
newsitem.headline: Japan railway group to unveil big office complex.

text.p: West Japan Railway Co will unveil a massive office and retailing complex in the historic city of Kyoto on Saturday in a bid to diversify from the slow-moving railway business.

Industry analysts say that JR West, like other companies that were formed by the dismantling of the former state-owned rail network, must find new sources of revenue in the face of expectations that its rail business is unlikely to grow.

"Management of the Kyoto station complex will serve as a touchstone for JR West, which is trying to expand the proportion of its business unrelated to train operation to about 20 to 30 percent in the years to come," Taku Mitsuma, an analyst at Yamaichi Research Institute of Securities and Economics Inc, said on Friday.

JR West president Masataka Ide has previously said that the company plans to eventually make businesses such as travel and retail account for 30 percent of total revenues, up from just 10 percent at present.

"The railway business has matured and the only thing JR West can do to keep its business growing is to expand into other operations," said Masahiro Kubo, an analyst at Daiwa Institute of Research Ltd.
"Therefore it is very important that it succeeds in this station complex business," he added.
The move comes at a time when much of the nation's real estate industry is still trying to recover from the collapse of the land "bubble" in the early 1990s.

Construction of the 150 billion yen ($1.31 billion) complex, the largest of its kind in Japan, began in late 1993 and is composed of a station building and other facilities including a 925-seat theatre, a major department store and a high-class hotel. All facilities will be inaugurated by September, JR West said.
Kyoto Station currently has an average of 150,000 users per day, but a JR West official said the company sees a daily flow of 160,000 people after September.

"We expect 80,000 customers daily in the commercial facilities (of the station complex). Additional trains for the route between Kyoto and Osaka, which start in September, would also boost the number of people who use the station," the official said.
Analysts, however, agreed that it would take time for the project to become profitable partly due to the substantial amount of capital invested.
JR West is one of the companies born of the former state-run Japan National Railways in 1987, after it was split up into six passenger train companies, one freight company and other firms.
It is not alone in its ambitious plans to move into real estate development. Another JR offshoot, JR Tokai, is planning a similar complex in Nagoya, Japan's third-largest metropolitan area.
